items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Like I don't doubt that an Ella Fitzgerald or a Sarah Vaughan or a Lena Horne, somebody like that, you know, after they were a big name, then he'd hire them to sing with the band, you know.

ctx.x: And he -- well, he had the knack -- it's a funny thing, he had the knack of knowing what to do with a band. He knew the people to get. So at the time, when Ella, Ella Fitzgerald came, he had -- he knew how to adjust to the commercial aspect, because he had to play her arrangements, which was the important thing then. But before that, when I was with him, the important thing was just playing stomping, knockdown jazz, and that was it. The more jazz we played the better, and of course at the Savoy you got all the…
Now, was anyone playing flute at that time, or was it -- was Wayman Carver the first?
